Date: 2026-07-03T16:12:00Z
Subject: OptiFind discovery - load sketch and next steps

Thanks team — quick recap from the call with OptiFind (Sarah + Eng):

- Primary goal: prove 99th-percentile inference latency < 450ms for typical query mix while keeping token cost below their target.
- Workload shape: mix of short queries (avg 12 tokens) and long summary requests (avg 620 tokens) with unpredictable daily bursts.
- Critical success criteria (high level): 95% of queries meet latency SLO in steady-state; system tolerates 3x baseline bursts for 2–5 minutes without >5% error rate or queue loss.

Action items I captured for POC planning:
1) Get concrete RPS / concurrency / burst numbers from OptiFind (they said they'd share sample logs).
2) Define acceptance test harness (we should provide a load script template + sample payloads).
3) Owners: Hannah to lead POC ops + telemetry; Laura to own eval metrics and quality checks; I’ll coordinate capacity.
4) Timeline: target 3-week POC after we receive payloads + access.

Attachment: I drafted a one-page MOP/ops checklist for the POC and a placeholder sample payload set — attaching here. Please review and I'll send to Sarah once we confirm owners and SLA asks.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — great talking with you earlier. Per Ben’s recap, we want to lock down the traffic profile so we can size the POC and build the acceptance harness. Can you confirm the numbers below and attach a 48–72 hour sample (CSV or JSON) if possible? I attached our MOP and a light load-template we use for POCs.

What we need from OptiFind (quick list):
- Steady-state RPS (average and 95th): numbers for weekdays and peak windows
- Expected concurrency (typical and peak)
- Token length distribution: short/medium/long buckets and typical percentiles (p50/p90/p99)
- Burst patterns: frequency, duration, and multiplier over baseline (e.g., 4x for 3 minutes)
- Any special request types (rerank, long summarization, embeddings) and their share of traffic

Acceptance checks we’ll run on POC:
- Latency SLOs by request class (we’ll propose thresholds after we see token distribution)
- Error rate and retry behavior under burst
- Cost per 1k tokens estimate across our suggestion set

If you can send the sample logs and any representative payloads (anonymous is fine) we’ll draft a concrete POC timeline + success criteria and circulate. Suggested owners: Hannah (POC ops / infra), Laura (eval / metrics), Ben (capacity + pricing).

Thanks — Hannah

Thanks Hannah — attaching the 72-hour sample you requested. Quick table of what the sample shows (we pulled representative traffic from last month):

- Steady-state: avg RPS = 18, p95 = 54
- Typical concurrency: 8 concurrent requests steady, peaks to 120 concurrent during marketing-driven spikes
- Token distribution: short (<=32 tokens) = 62%; medium (33–512) = 28%; long (>512) = 10%
  - p50 token length = 18, p90 = 410, p99 = 1,020
- Burst behavior: marketing campaigns trigger roughly 2–3 bursts/week; bursts last 2–6 minutes and spike to 4–7x baseline RPS (we saw 7x in last campaign)
- Request types: 82% short Q/A, 12% long summarization, 6% embeddings/rerank

Attachments included: optifind-load-matrix.csv (sample lines anonymized), sample-payloads.json (10 anonymized requests)

Notes: long summaries tend to be batched client-side; during bursts some clients disable background retries which helps avoid thundering. Let us know if you want additional fields in the sample (timestamps in ms, user-id hash).

—Sarah
Head of Product
OptiFind

Forwarding Sarah’s profile — this is the concrete traffic we need. My read + proposed POC plan below.

Quick interpretation:
- Baseline is low (avg 18 RPS) but bursts are the challenge: up to ~7x for short bursts and 120 concurrency means we need an architecture that handles high fan-out without long queues.
- Long-tail token sizes (p99 ~1k tokens) drive GPU memory / KV-cache sizing — we must validate memory footprints with representative models.

Proposed POC steps (3 weeks target once we have infra):
Week 0 (2 business days): ingest sample payloads and sanity checks; baseline single-node perf tests with their short/long mixes. Owner: Hannah.
Week 1 (5 business days): scale tests with burst emulation (4x, 7x) and concurrency probes; tune batching and KV-cache settings. Owner: Hannah + Ben (kernel/throughput tuning).
Week 2 (5 business days): SLA runs and acceptance tests (latency p95/p99 by class, error rates, token-cost estimate). Owner: Laura (metrics + evaluation) with ops support.
Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Short queries (<=32 tokens): p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms
- Medium queries (33–512 tokens): p95 < 450ms, p99 < 700ms
- Long queries (>512 tokens): p95 < 900ms, p99 < 1.5s
- Under 7x burst: overall error rate < 5% and no request loss (retries okay within backoff policy)

Logistics / prerequisites from OptiFind:
- Provide the 72-hour sample logs (got it) + an anonymized dataset with up to 500 long-summary requests for memory testing (ask Sarah).
- A contact for quick troubleshooting during burn-in windows (Sarah + Eng).

I'll draft a one-page POC plan to send to OptiFind with concrete schedule and test windows. Anything to add? Ben — pricing assumptions or capacity notes? Laura — do those acceptance thresholds make sense from your evaluation POV?

Hannah
